scope: Fourth photographic CL1 increment: versioned levels analysis with frozen Auto parameters, black/gray/white pickers, luminance point curves and parametric RGB/luminance curves in the existing process-5 stack. No complete CL/SF/R gate claim.
implemented: Three version-1 payloads: TonalLevels with optional analysis provenance, LuminanceCurve and ParametricCurve. Legacy Levels remains readable and retains its arithmetic; promotion occurs only for an explicit successful Auto/picker action. All versions are validated even when neutral.

Bounded analysis of at most 32768 uniformly distributed positions on the native input to the exact operator, after current crop/geometry and all preceding operators; target layer mask and opacity excluded. A 64-bin histogram accompanies RGB composite and per-channel controls.

Auto composite and independent channels freeze black/white values at the 1st/99th percentiles; existing gamma and output limits remain. Statistics exclude alpha below .95 and non-finite samples; insufficient opaque samples or degenerate ranges produce an atomic rejection.

Black, gray and white pickers address the selected channel and actual operator index. Gray solves signed-gamma parameters from an eligible positive sample toward its current luminance. Invalid gamma, range, coordinates and unavailable native pixels are rejected without a partial edit.

Analysis provenance records source SHA256, projected input recipe SHA256, geometry, dimensions, counts and optional picked position/RGB. Input/source changes invalidate the temporary cache; saved values never silently reanalyse on export.

Luminance point curves reuse the process-4 monotone point evaluator and add C(Y)-Y to each linear RGB channel. Parametric curves have four adjustable zones with quartic lifts, C1 boundaries, monotone response and RGB or additive-luminance application; extended negative/HDR tails are preserved.

Searchable IT/EN controls, targeted channel reset, explicit native analysis and completion/Esc, stale-input checks, exact neutral bypass, masked layer intensity and durable reopen/Undo/Redo through the existing recipe journal.

alpha_fixture.method: Deterministic synthetic raster: u=x/1199; v=y/799; R=.05+.9u; G=.08+.82v; B=.1+.8(.65u+.35v); A=1 for u<=.6, max(0,1-(u-.6)/.3) otherwise. Each component rounded to 8-bit. No user photograph or corpus original modified.

initial_probe.message: TrueRenderer: Auto livelli: campioni opachi insufficienti
initial_probe.expected_rejection: Fewer than 25% native input samples have alpha >= .95; Auto requires opaque statistics. The source also has constant RGB.

native_ui.scope: Native UI with isolated library and generated or explicit source; saved recipe, edited viewer/grid, optional RAW WB and Auto actions. Surface and export scope are reported separately. No universal RAW colour or physical display qualification.

native_levels_smoke.automation_note: The explicit --levels-auto-smoke helper freezes levels with the same native input projection/statistics before saving the fixture. This is not a manual click-through of the Auto/picker UI. The native report auto_actions field describes historical WB/tonal Auto actions, not this levels helper.

native_visual_review: Italian screenshot inspected: layer selection, layer intensity, parametric tool title, Luminance/RGB selector and curve graph are visible with the developed preview. The lower controls require vertical scrolling.

No full manual interaction campaign for the three new panels is claimed. Automated egui tests cover both languages, control opening without changes, channel-scoped reset, picker cancellation/selection, native-pixel eligibility and persistence.

limitations: Partial CL1 implementation. Direct photo interaction for curve points, curve neutralization/chroma variants, reusable looks and later packages remain open.

Levels Auto analyses the entire native developed crop excluding the target layer mask. The 1/99 percentile cutoffs and sampling bound are fixed; area pickers and configurable percentile policies are not provided.

Single-pixel gray neutralization rejects black/non-positive or out-of-range samples and unsupported gamma rather than silently clamping. Independent-channel Auto can change chromatic balance; the UI states this.
New operators and analysis run on CPU. GPU in the native surface report refers to presentation, not shader acceleration of these operators.

Synthetic PNG fixtures and four selected engine values do not qualify RAW camera decoding or calibrated colour. The first transparency probe was rejected for insufficient opaque pixels; the completed alpha matrix uses the explicitly documented new synthetic gradient.
Automated native screenshots/export are Italian; IT/EN interaction coverage is from egui regression tests. Full manual accessibility/VoiceOver and display-scale matrices remain unqualified.
No calibrated photographic/colorimetric, Windows, high-megapixel memory or latency campaign in this increment.

Ad hoc signing and XPC checks do not close release sandbox/assurance gates. Advanced selections, raster compositor/assets, retouching, models, batch and external-asset journal support remain separate future work.
